brief.scope: Security audit PR #57 lane/skeptic-write 75c4428 vs origin/dev. Files: ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py ops/conductor/tools/ladder.py. Hunt: writable_roots granted beyond check-tests out/; TMPDIR escaping the job; wait-reason treating a live wall as envelope=invalid.

findings.claim: Declared: read-role Codex must write out/SKEPTIC.md and temporary files while the snapshot remains read-only. Practiced: the argv selects `--sandbox read-only` and only configures `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots`; the installed Codex policy says read-only permits only reads and writable_roots applies to workspace-write. Fresh check-tests therefore remains unable to produce its deliverable or use TMPDIR, breaking the lane.
findings.reproduce: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=ops/devlane/dispatch python3 -c 'import launch,pathlib,shutil,subprocess; a=launch._argv("codex","m",None,"s","/job/prompt.txt",[],"read-only",writable_out=True); b=subprocess.check_output(["strings",str(pathlib.Path(shutil.which("codex")).resolve())],text=True); ro="Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `read-only`: The sandbox only permits reading files."; assert a[a.index("--sandbox")+1]=="read-only" and any("sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=" in x for x in a) and ro in b; print(a); print(ro)'

findings.claim: The new resumed check-tests argv appends `--sandbox` to `codex exec resume`, but that subcommand does not accept the option. Every resumed Codex check-tests attempt exits 2 during argument parsing before the model runs.
findings.reproduce: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=ops/devlane/dispatch python3 -c 'import launch,subprocess; a=launch._argv("codex","m",None,"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000","/job/prompt.txt",[],"read-only",resume=True,writable_out=True); p=subprocess.run(a,input="",text=True,capture_output=True); print(p.stderr); assert p.returncode==2 and "unexpected argument" in p.stderr and "--sandbox" in p.stderr'

findings.claim: TMPDIR is resolved without rejecting symlinks. Because a prior attempt controls out/, it can replace the initially empty out/tmp directory with a directory symlink; a resume accepts that symlink via mkdir(exist_ok=True) and exports its resolved target outside the job. This violates the job-directory boundary and can also make resumed tests fail under containment.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py").read_text(); out=Path(".claude/skills").resolve(); p=Path(".claude/skills/mate-php-environment-check"); assert "tmpdir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)" in s and "env[\"TMPDIR\"] = str(tmpdir.resolve())" in s and p.is_symlink(); p.mkdir(exist_ok=True); print(p.resolve()); assert not p.resolve().is_relative_to(out)'

envelope.note: Covered argv, shell/template, secret, path/ref, sandbox/record, wait-output, vendor-compatibility, and supply-chain surfaces. The nine changed files passed the repository secret scanner; no SQL, dependency pin, lockfile, or fetched-action surface changed. The new writable_out gate is check-tests-specific, and the ladder still classifies a live wait exit 2 as wall. Stateful unit suites could not run because the audit sandbox exposes no writable temporary directory; the non-mutating reproductions ran. Sandbox behavior was measured against installed codex-cli 0.153.2 after official documentation search returned no usable page. The session store was not read and the worktree remained clean.
